# STRATOS: Intelligence-Driven Aviation

> STRATOS is an aviation technology company based in Tallinn, Estonia. Its team brings 25+ years of experience in the aviation sector together with deep technology expertise, to build software for the way airlines operate. Two products for airline pilot training are live: STRATOS EBT/CBTA and STRATOS TMS.

Canonical page: https://stratos-ida.com/

## Who we are

STRATOS pairs 25+ years of experience in the aviation sector (flight operations, crew training, regulation and oversight, seen from inside the airline) with deep expertise in software engineering, data and analytics, delivered as secure systems an airline can rely on every day. What it builds follows how airlines are run and regulated.

- **One shared foundation:** every product is set up to the airline's own manuals and authority, and works from the same records.

## Direction

An airline runs on connected disciplines. STRATOS is building technology for each of them, one domain at a time, on one shared foundation. It started with training.

## The training solution

Two connected products for airline pilot training: one measures how well pilots perform, the other keeps every pilot current. Airlines can take one, or both on a single pilot record.

### STRATOS EBT/CBTA: every grade consistent, every skill measured

Evidence-based training and assessment, graded by the ICAO, IATA and EASA method on forms built from the airline's own manual.

- Nine ICAO/IATA competencies and all 73 observable behaviours
- Day 2 training planned from the pilot's Day 1 evidence
- Trends by pilot, cohort, fleet and instructor

Details: https://stratos-ida.com/ebt-cbta

### STRATOS TMS: every pilot current, every renewal planned

The training management system: validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one place.

- Every licence, medical, check and course tracked live
- Renewals planned months ahead, pilots reminded before anything lapses
- One digital file per pilot, ready for the inspector

Details: https://stratos-ida.com/tms

### One pilot record: entered once, never re-typed

For airlines that take both, the products share one crew list, one pilot record and one login.

- A graded check updates the record and sets the next expiry
- Compliance and competence side by side for the Director
- One audit trail across both products

Built on ICAO, IATA and EASA guidance, set up to each airline's manuals and authority.

# About STRATOS

> STRATOS is an aviation technology company based in Tallinn, Estonia. Its team pairs 25 years of experience in the aviation sector with deep technology expertise. It is developing technology across the airline and started with training: STRATOS EBT/CBTA and STRATOS TMS are live today.

Canonical page: https://stratos-ida.com/about

- **Vision:** Unifying fragmented data into a single source of operational intelligence and continuous oversight.
- **Mission:** Turning complex aviation data into connected intelligence that raises safety, performance and continuous improvement.

## Who we are

- **Experience:** 25 years of experience in the aviation sector. Flight operations, crew training, regulation and oversight, seen from inside the airline.
- **Expertise:** Deep technology. Software engineering, data and analytics, delivered as secure systems an airline can rely on every day.
- **Base:** Tallinn, Estonia. An aviation technology company working with airlines and their authorities.
- **In production:** AlMasria Universal Airlines. Founding reference client: 120+ pilots and 250+ cabin crew, with more than 14,000 grades recorded to date.

## Products

- **STRATOS EBT/CBTA** (live): competency assessment and training records. It captures, grades and analyses evaluation data against the ICAO/IATA competency framework.
- **STRATOS TMS** (live): validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one system, sharing one crew list and one pilot record with STRATOS EBT/CBTA.
- **What they are not:** neither product delivers e-learning courses. They record, plan and analyse training and assessment.

## Direction: one domain at a time, on one shared foundation

An airline runs on connected disciplines. STRATOS is building technology for each of them. Training is live; the next domains follow on the same foundation.

1. **Training (live):** STRATOS EBT/CBTA for competency assessment and STRATOS TMS for training management, on one pilot record.
2. **Safety & Compliance (next):** occurrence reporting and audit findings tied back to the competency evidence behind them.
3. **Flight Operations (next):** crew qualification, currency and rostering constraints in the same record as training.
4. **Maintenance & Engineering (next):** technical training and authorisation tracking on the shared competency framework.
5. **Network Planning (next):** capacity and crew readiness modelled against the training pipeline.

## Core strategic pillars

- **Connected Intelligence:** elevating passive records into active, cross-departmental forecasting and risk assessment.
- **Architectural Scalability:** a unified technological infrastructure designed to adapt and expand alongside evolving global aviation needs.
- **Operational Clarity:** complex industry data delivered through intuitive, high-visibility interfaces that minimize administrative friction.

## Brand values

1. **Absolute Precision:** data treated with the rigor required on the flight deck.
2. **Architectural Foresight:** every module and workflow engineered to integrate into a wider ecosystem.
3. **Actionable Clarity:** complex metrics distilled into insights that accelerate decisions.
4. **Continuous Integration:** the feedback loop between operational execution, data evaluation and systemic improvement.

## How we work with you: set up from your manuals

STRATOS staff onboard each airline from its own manuals. STRATOS builds the airline's check forms from its paper forms, sets its grading scale and document control, and configures the platform to its authority. Building forms is part of the implementation service, not a self-serve builder. Forms stay as they are, whether they start on paper or in digital form. Support and maintenance are included.

# STRATOS solutions: EBT/CBTA and TMS for airline pilot training

> Two connected products for airline pilot training. STRATOS EBT/CBTA grades competency by the ICAO, IATA and EASA method. STRATOS TMS keeps every pilot current and every renewal planned. Both are configured to each airline's own training manual and authority, not tied to one regulator, and every airline's data is isolated from every other's.

Canonical page: https://stratos-ida.com/solutions

## 1. STRATOS EBT/CBTA (competence): every grade consistent, every skill measured

Evidence-based training and assessment for airline recurrent pilot training. Grading, training planning, analytics and records in one system, built on the ICAO, IATA and EASA method.

- 9 ICAO/IATA pilot competencies · 73 observable behaviours in IATA wording · 329 IATA scenarios for Day 2 planning · as many forms as the airline uses, built natively rule for rule
- Modules: competency grading (IATA lowest-of-three rule), forms built from the airline's manual, Day 2 planning, three-altitude analytics and fleet risk board, instructor standardisation, signed PDF and append-only audit log, EBT stage support (conventional checking native; Mixed EBT native for pilot assessment)

Full detail: https://stratos-ida.com/ebt-cbta

## 2. STRATOS TMS (compliance): every pilot current, every renewal planned

The training management system. Validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one place, configured to the airline's Operations Manual and authority.

- 5 status levels checked daily; the worst item sets the pilot's file · 3-year recurrent cycle run per pilot · KPI targets set per airline
- Modules: validity control, expiry engine (OM-D rules, renewal windows, end-of-month counting), 3-year plan and monthly load, recurrent cycle, digital pilot file, reports (MEETS / WATCH / BELOW), pilot portal & email notices

Full detail: https://stratos-ida.com/tms

## 3. How they work together: one crew list, one pilot record, one login

For airlines that take both, every step of a pilot's proficiency check writes to the same record, so nothing is typed twice:

1. **TMS plans the check:** the expiry engine sees the operator proficiency check falls due inside the planning window; the pilot is placed in a simulator group and emailed the assignment, with a reminder before the session. An audit entry is written.
2. **EBT/CBTA grades the check:** grades by the airline's rules, a signed PDF generated on submission, live fleet analytics updated.
3. **TMS updates the record:** the completed, graded session updates the TMS record with no re-typing. The expiry engine recalculates the check from its rule (e.g. 6 calendar months, end of month) and the plan drops the pilot from that month. The pilot portal shows the new expiry; the office is notified.
4. **The Director sees both:** validity and competence for the same pilot, fleet and period, side by side. Board-ready reports and an audit pack are one click away.

### What is shared, and who writes it

- **Crew list:** imported from the crew system and matched to every training record; imports are reconciled so gaps are found before the auditor finds them.
- **Pilot record:** the single record both products update (licences, medicals, checks, courses, grades and documents, per pilot).
- **Training rules:** configured per airline by admins; used by the TMS expiry engine and the EBT/CBTA grading engine.
- **Competency grades:** with the observable behaviours, TEM outcome and instructor narrative behind each one.
- **Expiries:** calculated by the expiry engine from the latest record and its rule, never typed; every expiry traced to its rule.
- **Documents:** scans and certificates filed to the pilot, flagged when missing or outdated, plus a signed PDF for every evaluation.
- **Audit trail:** every change, who, when and how it was entered; every save backed up automatically.

Every airline's data is isolated from every other's. Pilot and cabin-crew records are kept separate at the database level, and the data stays the airline's, exportable in full at any time.

## One platform, every role

One login. Each user sees and changes only what their role allows, in both products. Every action is logged.

- **Training Director & admins:** see everything and set the rules: rules, settings and users; KPI reports by fleet and period; the full audit trail; fleet dashboards and the risk board; instructor consistency; policies, standards and alerts.
- **Training office / coordinators:** run the daily work: record training for one pilot or a class; update crew, plan groups, book sessions; import and export.
- **Instructors:** grade on forms built from the airline's manual; plan Day 2 from the pilot's Day 1.
- **Pilots & cabin crew:** self-service, no calls to the office: portal for licence, medical, renewals and upcoming training; email before each expiry; rate each session through a short link, no login; results framed as coaching, not discipline.

## Implementation: four stages, about five weeks

Target timeline from receiving the airline's manual, records and forms. The airline names one owner; STRATOS does the setup.

1. **Stage 1:** the airline provides its Operations Manual and training manual, current records and forms, and one named owner. STRATOS reviews them and maps every record to a pilot. Output: scope and plan agreed.
2. **Stage 2:** the airline answers mapping questions. STRATOS moves records from Excel, paper or the old system, builds forms from the manual and recalculates every expiry. Output: records migrated, forms built.
3. **Stage 3:** the airline reviews rules and standards. STRATOS loads the crew list, creates accounts, sets up training rules and standards, and reconciles against the source data. Output: Director sign-off.
4. **Stage 4:** the team attends training on live data. STRATOS trains users on their own data and switches on notices and dashboards. Output: expiries, grades and dashboards live.

The airline owns the programme and keeps every regulatory obligation; the instructor sets every final grade and STRATOS never overwrites it. Authorities approve programmes, not software.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can we start with one product?**
Yes. Take STRATOS TMS, STRATOS EBT/CBTA, or both. Each runs on its own. Together they share one crew list, one login and one pilot record, so a graded check updates the next expiry with no re-typing.

**We already use another platform.**
STRATOS moves you across. Your forms are digitised, and your past grades and training records are moved into the new system. The migration is done by STRATOS.

**Do we have to change our forms?**
No. If you have a training manual but no digital forms, STRATOS builds the forms from your manual, rule for rule. If you already have forms you want to keep, STRATOS implements those exactly: same structure, same scoring logic, same sign-off chain, so instructors see what they already know, digitised.

**Will our pilots accept it?**
Results are framed as coaching, not discipline. The instructor sets every grade and STRATOS never overwrites it. Pilots also see their own status in the portal instead of asking the office.

**What happens to our data?**
It stays yours: isolated from every other airline and exportable in full at any time. Pilot and cabin-crew records are held separately at the database level rather than hidden in the interface, so a security review or an auditor gets a verifiable answer about isolation.

**Does it replace our LMS or rostering?**
No. STRATOS works alongside both. Rostering stays where it is, and STRATOS does not deliver e-learning. Connecting the TMS to an existing LMS is on the roadmap: where the LMS supports module export, its learning modules can be embedded in the TMS.

**Is the software approved by the authority?**
Authorities approve programmes, not software. STRATOS supports your compliance with EASA and your national rules, and the airline keeps every regulatory obligation.

**How long does implementation take?**
Four stages, about five weeks, from receiving your manual, records and forms. You name one owner; STRATOS does the setup.

## Three steps, one decision

Agree a pilot project: one fleet, the products you need, and success measures set in advance. Then share your manuals, records and forms, and go live. Contact: https://stratos-ida.com/contact · info@stratos-ida.com

# STRATOS EBT/CBTA: EBT/CBTA assessment platform for airlines

> From paper records to performance intelligence. STRATOS EBT/CBTA grades every check against the ICAO nine-competency framework on the airline's own forms, and turns every submission into pilot, cohort and fleet analytics. Built on the ICAO, IATA and EASA method (also ECAA). Live, in daily production at AlMasria Universal Airlines.

Canonical page: https://stratos-ida.com/ebt-cbta
For: Training Directors, Heads of Training and TRE/TRI leads.

Key numbers: 9 ICAO core competencies · 73 observable behaviours (IATA wording and numbering) · 329 IATA scenarios for Day 2 planning · 3 analytical altitudes (micro, macro, trend) · 4 one-click outcomes on submission.

## The problem: today's tools record the grade, analysis is still done by hand

EBT/CBTA expects grades derived from observed behaviour, trends tracked across the whole pilot population, and proof that every instructor grades to one standard.

- **Paper and spreadsheets (records, not insight):** grades are cut off from the competency framework; every cohort review and audit response is assembled by hand, and a lost file is a gap in a pilot's record. Result: trends surface too late.
- **An existing ETR system (built to file grades):** designed to store training records, with competencies added later. Instructors still work out competency grades by hand, so consistency depends on the individual. Result: instructor variance unseen.
- **Tools built for the methodology (thin where it matters):** analysis usually stops at the individual pilot; cohort trends, fleet risk and instructor standardisation stay manual, and fixed templates make airlines adapt to the tool. Result: insight stays manual.

## Positioning: the EBT/CBTA layer

STRATOS EBT/CBTA sits alongside the airline's LMS and can be integrated with STRATOS TMS.

- **LMS (adjacent system):** delivers e-learning content (course hosting, SCORM playback, knowledge checks). STRATOS does not deliver e-learning.
- **STRATOS EBT/CBTA:** calculates competency grades against the ICAO nine-competency framework using the airline's own scoring rules. A signed PDF per evaluation, a permanent per-pilot history with a full edit audit trail, and pilot, cohort and fleet analytics.
- **STRATOS TMS (integrates):** validity, planning and scheduling, on one pilot record.
- **Responsibilities:** the airline owns every regulatory obligation (implementation plan, safety risk assessment, authority submissions). STRATOS supports it: captures evidence, recommends grades, applies the correct standard and raises policy flags. The instructor decides and sets the final grade; any override needs a written reason. STRATOS never overwrites it.

## Native to the EBT transition

Whether an airline is starting EBT or already running it, STRATOS supports the programme at its current stage and carries it to the next, on one platform. Each airline sets its own stage, with a start date, and moves up with the same records, pilots and history. Each check is graded under the stage in force on its date.

- **Conventional checking ("train, then check"):** native.
- **Mixed EBT ("check, then train"):** native for pilot assessment, live. A Day 1 proficiency check comes first; Day 2 training is planned from its findings, with ranked scenarios from the 329 in IATA's EBT workbook. The nine competencies are graded 1–5 as the airline's manual defines, with optional observable behaviours and TEM outcomes. Same engine, cycles and modules are live; equivalency tables and line-check intervals are on the roadmap.
- **Enhanced EBT:** needs flight data (future plan).

## On submission: one click, four things happen automatically

1. **Calculates competency grades:** nine competencies graded on the airline's scale, following its sign-off chain. Each grade is derived from observed behaviours by the IATA lowest-of-three method.
2. **Generates a signed PDF report.**
3. **Adds a permanent record** to the pilot's history, with the observed behaviours behind each grade.
4. **Feeds live fleet analytics:** fleet dashboard and cohort comparison updated.

## Grading engine

- Every check graded against the nine ICAO/IATA pilot competencies (KNO application of knowledge, PRO procedures & compliance, COM communication, FPA flight path automation, FPM flight path manual, LTW leadership & teamwork, PSD problem solving & decision making, SAW situation awareness, WLM workload management), with all 73 observable behaviours in IATA's own wording and numbering.
- Each exercise is mapped to the competencies it mainly tests and those it supports.
- Recommended grade by the IATA lowest-of-three rule: how many OBs, how often, TEM outcome.
- "Insufficient evidence" instead of a number when evidence is thin.
- Any item graded 1 or 2 needs observable-behaviour evidence.
- The instructor decides; a different final grade needs a written reason.

## Forms: built from your manual

Rebuilt from the airline's own forms at onboarding: items, grading scale per section, attempts, TEM-applicable items and competency mapping, printed in the layout of the airline's paper form.

- Simulator check (OPC/LPC), line check, training & evaluation, cabin crew, remedial training
- The airline's scale per section: S/U/N-A, PASS/FAIL or 1–5
- First and second attempts recorded

## Day 2 planning

The next session is built from what the last check found. The recurrent programme is planned as cycles, modules and two-day sessions, each with an assigned instructor.

- Open a pilot's Day 1 and see which OBs were demonstrated
- Choose the competencies to develop
- IATA Appendix G.V scenarios ranked by coverage, tagged primary or secondary
- A record of who chose what and when

## Analytics at three altitudes

- **Micro (the single evaluation):** a close look category by category, behaviour by behaviour. Numeric or categorical, detected automatically.
- **Macro (the cohort):** compare every pilot in a class, rank or aircraft type. Tells an individual issue from a programme one (one pilot struggled, or the entire class did), which is the input EBT expects in the next recurrent cycle.
- **Trend (the pilot over time):** a chronological view of one pilot's history: improving, plateauing or slipping.
- **Fleet risk board:** a short, ranked list of the pilots to review first, each linked to the pilot's record and trend view.

## Instructor standardisation

Each instructor's average grade is updated with every submission and compared with the fleet mean, with a tolerance band, so standards stay consistent. Supports instructor standardisation in Mixed EBT. Trainees rate each session through a short link (QR), no login. Director dashboard for instructor ratings.

## Records and audit

Submitting a form calculates the grades, generates a signed PDF, adds a permanent record and feeds live analytics at once. Every edit after submission is logged in an append-only audit trail. Below-standard alerts email the training managers. Records export for IOSA and the airline's authority.

## AI coaching assistant

For pilots with two or more checks, a plain-language coaching and remediation summary. Gated on history, just-culture framing, Director-only switch.

## Product status

**Live:** own forms (simulator, remedial, line check, cabin crew) · grading engine (lowest-of-three, your scale) · reports & signatures (signed PDF, audit trail) · micro/macro/trend analytics · fleet dashboard (KPIs, risk ranking, TEM themes) · instructor comparison · AI coaching & fleet report (Director-gated) · trainee feedback (QR, no login) · currency & validity (3-year cycle expiry alerts).

**Planned next:** malfunction and approach equivalency tables · baseline line-check intervals · instructor Mixed EBT.

**Future plan:** Enhanced EBT with flight-data integration · type rating, MPL and ab initio · pilot self-service · offline app.

## Onboarding: fitted to the airline

STRATOS develops forms from the airline's training manual, with competency mapping, OBs and TEM, or digitises existing forms exactly as they are. Support and maintenance included.

1. **Discovery:** the training manual and any existing evaluation forms, digital or paper.
2. **Build:** each form developed from the manual, or existing forms digitised as they are.
3. **Configure:** rosters loaded, instructor and Director accounts created, departments set.
4. **Go-live:** grading, reporting and analytics run from the first submission.

Handbook (PDF): https://stratos-ida.com/uploads/STRATOS_EBT_CBTA_Handbook.pdf · Contact: https://stratos-ida.com/contact

# STRATOS TMS: pilot training management system

> Every pilot current. Every renewal planned. STRATOS TMS puts validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one system, configured to the airline's Operations Manual (OM-D) and national authority. It connects to STRATOS EBT/CBTA for airlines that subscribe to it. Live.

Canonical page: https://stratos-ida.com/tms
For: Directors of Training, Heads of Training and Crew Training Managers.

Key numbers: 5 status levels, checked daily · worst item sets the pilot's status · 3-year recurrent cycle, run per pilot · KPI targets set per airline.

## What changes: fragmented becomes one training system

- **Time:** hours lost to admin. The same dates are typed into spreadsheets, forms and emails; staff check records instead of planning.
- **Errors:** one typo, one lapse. A wrong date or a missed renewal stays hidden until the roster is built or an inspector asks for the file.
- **Legacy tools:** built for another era. Older systems often run on one PC, send no reminders and do not connect to rostering or competency data.

The data already exists. What is missing is one modern system that keeps it current automatically.

## A daily action list, not a spreadsheet

Filter by status, then record a renewal. The expiry is recalculated from the rule and the pilot leaves the list. Items tracked include OPC (operator proficiency check), LPC (licence proficiency check), LC (line check), CRM (crew resource management), DG (dangerous goods), SEP (emergency & safety equipment), class 1 medical and passport.

## Validity control: the worst item sets the status

Every licence, medical, check and course is scored against the airline's own rule. A pilot's overall status is their worst item, so one lapsed check flags the whole file. Status follows the airline's rules, for example: GREEN over 60 days · YELLOW 60 days or less · RED under 30 days · EXPIRED · MISSING.

- Daily action list by fleet, status and item
- Data-gap report for mandatory items with no record
- Red and expired items feed the renewal plan and pilot notices automatically

## Modules: one platform, every training workflow

### Expiry engine: calculated, not typed
Validity periods, renewal windows and expiry counting configured to the airline's OM-D and national authority. Every expiry is traced to its rule; the new expiry is suggested from the rule and reviewed before saving.
- Calendar-month and end-of-month counting
- Renewal windows keep the original expiry
- Medical interval set per pilot, by age and operation
- Check spacing validated against OM limits

### Planning: demand known months ahead
Every renewal placed by expiry and lead time, with the reason shown for each month. Overdue items are pulled into the first planning month automatically.
- 3-year renewal plan by month; monthly load shows peaks before they happen
- Simulator groups aligned to each pilot's check expiry; OPC + SIM shown as one booking
- Email on booking, change and cancellation, plus a reminder

### Recurrent cycle: the 3-year cycle, run per pilot
Phases, base-month groups and checklists built from the airline's recurrent programme. A passed check or course writes the completion and new expiry to the pilot's record.
- Seasonal phases, e.g. cold and hot weather operations
- Base-month groups built from each pilot's check expiry
- Each item: date, result, score, attempts, remedial, simulator hours, feedback
- Lapse warnings for checks that expire before the plan
- Cycle KPIs: completion, on-time, first-pass and remedial rates

### Records: one digital file per pilot
Records, documents and the audit trail, ready for the inspector at any time. Crew-system imports are reconciled against training records, so gaps are found before the auditor finds them.
- Record one pilot or a full class in one step
- Documents flagged when missing or out of date
- Pilot file in six folders; automatic backups; encrypted ZIP export for an inspection
- Every change logged: who, when and how

### Reports: training performance, measured
Monthly, quarterly and yearly reports for the Director, by fleet and activity. Every KPI target is set by the airline's training department.
- Training compliance, on-time renewal and first-pass rate
- Overdue items and data gaps
- First-pass and remedial training rates; simulator utilisation against plan; instructor observations
- MEETS / WATCH / BELOW status, export to PDF or Excel

### Pilot portal & notices: pilots see their own status
- Licence, medical, ratings, qualifications and upcoming training
- Email ahead of each expiry, e.g. 45 days, passports 90
- Planned, changed or cancelled training by email
- Daily digest of changes and expiries for admins

## How it works: one loop, no re-keying

A record entered once updates the plan, the pilot and the reports: results entered once → expiry recalculated, certificate filed (EBT/CBTA grade linked for subscribers) → renewal plan and monthly load rebuilt → pilots booked into simulator, classroom and checks with email notice → live validity, KPIs and audit-ready pilot files for the Director.

## Integration with STRATOS EBT/CBTA

For airlines subscribed to STRATOS EBT/CBTA, both systems share one crew list, one pilot record and one login. A completed, graded session updates the TMS record and the next expiry, with no double entry. The Director sees validity, competency trends and instructor concordance side by side, per pilot and per fleet. On the roadmap: connecting to the airline's existing LMS (STRATOS does not build an LMS).

## Implementation & migration: we move your records, you sign off

From Excel, paper or a legacy TMS, STRATOS does the full migration and implementation. The training department reviews and approves; it does not re-key records.

- **We migrate:** Excel training sheets, paper records, legacy TMS data, crew master & rosters, training history, certificates & scans, licences & medicals, simulator & check records.
- **We configure:** training rules from the Operations Manual; the recurrent programme (courses, phases, simulator cycle).
- **We validate:** reconciliation against the source data; Director sign-off before go-live.

Every record mapped to the pilot, every expiry recalculated, every document filed in the pilot's digital file. Users are trained on the live system with their own data.

## Three steps, one decision

1. **Live demo:** the TMS shown on a sample of your own crew and training data.
2. **Data & scope intake:** records, rules and manuals shared; quote sized to your crew list.
3. **Migrate · go live:** records migrated, rules configured, team trained, live across the fleet.

Contact: https://stratos-ida.com/contact · info@stratos-ida.com

# STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook (full text)

Source PDF: https://stratos-ida.com/uploads/STRATOS_EBT_CBTA_Handbook.pdf

STRATOS
INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN AVIATION
EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
What it is, how it's built for your airline, and every module inside it — explained without the
technical jargon.
Prepared for internal and client use
September 2026
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
1. What Is STRATOS EBT/CBTA?
EBT/CBTA is a training methodology. STRATOS EBT/CBTA is the platform built natively to run
it.
It helps to separate two things that sound similar but aren't. “EBT/CBTA” is not a product — it's an
internationally recognized training methodology: a set of rules, from ICAO and IATA, for how pilots and
cabin crew should be evaluated against defined competencies instead of a simple pass/fail mark.
“STRATOS EBT/CBTA” is the software product built to run that methodology day to day for an airline.
The distinction matters because most training-record tools were not built this way. They were built as
general-purpose record-keeping tools first, and the EBT/CBTA competency structure was bolted on
afterward. STRATOS was built the other way around: the grading logic, the data model, and every screen in
the product are constructed directly from the EBT/CBTA framework from day one. It is native to the
methodology, not adapted to it.
What problem it actually solves
Very few airlines today are still purely on paper. In practice, most fill out training evaluations using a basic
Electronic Training Records (ETR) tool, plain Excel spreadsheets, or an older legacy system that was never
designed around EBT/CBTA competencies in the first place. All three approaches share the same weakness:
they can store a grade, but they cannot natively calculate it against the competency framework, and they
cannot turn a stack of individual evaluations into fleet-wide intelligence.
STRATOS EBT/CBTA is built to replace all three of those options — paper, spreadsheets, and generic
legacy ETR systems alike — with a single platform where every evaluation form, grading rule, and
analytics view is native to the EBT/CBTA methodology itself.
The moment an examiner submits a form, STRATOS automatically:
• Calculates the pilot's competency grades using the airline's official EBT/CBTA scoring rules
• Generates a clean, signed PDF report of the evaluation
• Adds the result to that pilot's full training history
• Feeds the result into fleet-wide analytics dashboards the Training Director can see in real time
Where it's built and proven
STRATOS is the product of an Egypt/Estonia-based aviation technology venture, in daily production use at
El Masria Universal Airlines (“AlMasria”), which remains the platform's founding reference client and
proving ground.
1.1 What the Product Is Built On
Beyond the feature list, four working principles run through every module in this handbook — they're the
reason the product looks the way it does:
• Absolute precision — aviation data gets the same rigor a flight deck demands. Grading rules,
competency mappings, and regulatory alignment are treated as non-negotiable, not approximated.
Page 2
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
• Architectural foresight — every module, form, and database structure is built to plug into a wider,
future-proof system — which is why pilot and cabin-crew evaluation already coexist on one platform,
and why new modules can be added without reworking what already exists.
• Actionable clarity — complex aviation metrics are deliberately distilled into high-visibility insights
— a risk ranking, a heatmap, a coaching summary — rather than raw numbers a Director has to
interpret alone.
• Continuous integration — the platform is built around a feedback loop, not a one-way record: an
evaluation feeds analytics, analytics feed coaching and risk flags, and trainee feedback feeds back into
how training itself is run.
1.2 What This Means for Your Training Department
A Training Director doesn't need another records system — there's usually already one, even if it's just a
shared spreadsheet. What's actually in short supply is defensible evidence, standardization across the
examiner pool, and hours back in the training department's week. That's the gap STRATOS EBT/CBTA is
built to close:
• Audit-ready by design — every grade traces back to the specific observed behavior it came from, so
an ECAA, GACA, or IOSA audit is answered with real evidence on demand, not reconstructed from
memory the week before an inspection.
• A standardized examiner pool — examiner concordance (Section 6.5) gives the Training Director
objective, ongoing evidence that grading standards are applied evenly across every TRE and TRI —
usually the first thing an inspector asks about and the hardest thing to prove on paper.
• Protects a just, non-punitive safety culture — this is the philosophy EBT/CBTA itself is built on:
competency data is there to identify training needs, not to single out individual pilots. STRATOS keeps
that intent intact by turning results into coaching and remedial guidance rather than a disciplinary
record.
• Time back for the training department — an evaluation that used to mean a paper trail, a manual
write-up, and a spreadsheet update now produces its own report, its own record, and its own analytics
the moment it's submitted.
• A record that holds up beyond the training department — the same audit trail that satisfies a
regulator also stands up for insurance review and internal safety investigations, because it was captured
at the time of the evaluation, not reconstructed afterward.
2. The Methodology Behind the Product
These are the industry terms worth understanding once, since the rest of the handbook builds on them.
EBT — Evidence-Based Training
EBT is ICAO's methodology for evaluating pilots against a defined set of core competencies — things like
Application of Procedures, Communication, Leadership & Teamwork, Problem Solving, and Workload
Management — instead of a single pass/fail mark for a whole session. STRATOS grades against the full
nine competencies in this framework.
Page 3
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
CBTA — Competency-Based Training and Assessment
CBTA is IATA's parallel methodology, applied more broadly across training and assessment. “EBT/CBTA”
together is the modern, competency-focused standard that STRATOS is built natively around.
ETR — Electronic Training Records
This is the precise category for the product itself: a digital system of record for training evaluations, built
around the EBT/CBTA methodology. It is not a Learning Management System (LMS) — it doesn't deliver
e-learning courses — and it is not (yet) a full Training Management System (TMS) — it doesn't handle
scheduling or rostering. What it does, it does natively and deeply: capturing, grading, and analyzing real
evaluation data against the international competency framework, in a way that generic ETR tools,
spreadsheets, and legacy systems were never built to do.
3. Who Uses STRATOS
The platform is built around three roles, each with a different screen and a different job:
• Training Director — sees everything: every pilot, every examiner, every form, fleet-wide dashboards,
and administrative controls. Manages user accounts and oversees the training program as a whole.
• Examiner (TRE/TRI/Instructor) — fills out evaluation forms during and after a simulator session,
line check, or cabin-crew assessment, applying the same competency standard the rest of the examiner
pool is held to. Sees their own evaluation history and the pilots they've assessed.
• Trainee (Pilot / Cabin Crew) — is the subject of the evaluation, and participates directly through the
trainee feedback loop (Module 6.6) after each training session.
Pilot records and cabin-crew records are kept securely separate within the system (each department only
sees its own data), even though both run on the same platform.
Page 4
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
4. The Evaluation Forms
Everything in STRATOS starts with one of the airline's official evaluation forms, digitized exactly as the
regulator and the airline already use them. These forms are built directly from real, currently-in-use
Egyptian airline documentation — not a generic template — which makes them some of the most detailed,
operationally accurate EBT-aligned evaluation forms running at any Egyptian carrier today.
F-001
Simulator Check
The periodic evaluation a pilot completes in the flight simulator, graded directly across all
nine core EBT competencies.
F-002
Line Check
An in-flight evaluation of a pilot during real operations. Structured into four sections —
Threat & Error Management, CRM/Non-Technical Skills, EBT Competency, and
Knowledge — with the full nine-competency model inside the EBT section.
F-003
Training / Evaluation Monitor
An earlier, ongoing training-monitor form used alongside F-001 and F-002. It still runs on
the airline's original technical and CRM category structure and is being carried forward
toward the same nine-competency model as the other two forms.
F-077
Cabin Crew Assessment
The annual evaluation for cabin crew, using a categorical scoring framework suited to cabin
operations rather than the pilot nine-competency model — by design, not as a gap.
4.1 What's Actually Inside a Form
Every form follows the same underlying anatomy, whichever of the four it is:
• Header details — pilot or crew member, rank, aircraft type, date, examiner, and session type, captured
once and reused everywhere that record appears.
• Competency grading blocks — for F-001 and F-002, this is the nine EBT competencies; for F-077,
the cabin-specific categorical scale; for F-003, the legacy technical and CRM categories. Each block is
scored using the airline's official rules, not a generic average.
• Threat & Error Management (TEM) — a dedicated section capturing any threats or errors that came
up during the session and how the crew managed them — a core requirement of the EBT/CBTA
methodology, not an optional add-on.
• Observed-behavior detail — the specific behaviors the examiner actually saw, not just a final number
— this is what lets STRATOS later explain why a grade was what it was.
• Free-text comments — space for the examiner's own notes and context on the session, tied directly to
the record.
Page 5
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
• Sign-off block — the formal approval step (examiner, trainee, inspector, and operations training
manager where required) that closes the record out.
Page 6
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
5. How We Set Up STRATOS for an Airline
The platform is implemented around the airline's own standards — not the other way around.
An airline coming to STRATOS starts from one of two places, and the platform is built to handle both
without asking the airline to change its own paperwork or standards:
• The airline has a training manual but no digital forms yet — we take the airline's own Operations
Manual and governing training documents and build the digital forms directly from them, matching the
airline's exact structure, wording, and scoring rules.
• The airline already has its own forms it wants to keep using — we implement those exact forms on
the platform as they are, so examiners see the same layout and standards they already know, just
digitized.
Either way, the outcome is the same: the airline gets a platform that speaks its own language from day one,
not a generic tool it has to adapt to.
5.1 The Setup Stages
1. Documentation intake — we collect the airline's training manual and/or its existing paper or digital
evaluation forms.
2. Form build — our team recreates each form on the platform, rule for rule: the same competency
structure, the same scoring logic, the same sign-off requirements as the source document.
3. Data and account setup — pilot and crew rosters, examiner and Director accounts, and department
structure (pilots vs. cabin crew) are entered into the system.
4. Go-live — the platform is ready to use instantly. Examiners start filling out the same forms they
already know how to use, now digital — with grading, reporting, and analytics running automatically
from the first submitted evaluation.
Why this matters
Because the forms are built from the airline's own manual or existing paperwork rather than a fixed
template, onboarding doesn't require the airline to redesign its training standards to fit the software — the
software is fitted to the airline.
Page 7
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
6. The Modules — What STRATOS Actually Does
STRATOS is organized into modules. Each one covers a distinct part of the training-evaluation
workflow — and the analytics layer is where the platform goes furthest beyond a digital filing
cabinet.
6.1 Digital Evaluation Forms
The starting point for every record in the system — F-001, F-002, F-003, and F-077, built to the airline's
own structure as described in Section 5. Built-in validation reduces the data-entry errors common with
paper and spreadsheets, and every form records the specific behaviors observed, not just a final number.
6.2 Competency Grading Engine
The calculation layer behind every form. Once an examiner enters their observations, STRATOS
automatically works out the pilot's grade on each competency, using the airline's official EBT/CBTA rules
— including the “lowest of three” principle used across the industry, where a competency grade reflects the
weakest of: how many good behaviors were demonstrated, how consistently, and how any threats or errors
were handled.
• Grades run on a five-band scale, from S1 (Unsatisfactory) to S5 (Excellent)
• A borderline or failing grade on any competency automatically flags the pilot for mandatory remedial
training
• The same grading logic is applied consistently every time — removing the inconsistency that creeps in
with manual, spreadsheet-based scoring
6.3 Instant Reports & Records
The moment a form is submitted, STRATOS generates a polished, professional PDF report of the
evaluation — ready to file, print, or share — and stores it permanently against that pilot's record, with a full
audit trail of any later edits.
• A pending-approval step before a submitted evaluation becomes final, so a Director can review before
it's locked in
• Post-submission editing is supported when a correction is genuinely needed — the PDF report is
automatically regenerated to match
• Deleting a record follows a controlled, cascading process with a detailed audit trail, rather than a record
simply disappearing
6.4 The AI Coaching Assistant
For pilots with enough evaluation history, an AI assistant reviews the pilot's latest result alongside their past
performance and drafts a plain-language coaching summary — explaining what the trend shows and what to
focus on next, in words a Training Director or the pilot can immediately understand.
• Looks at patterns across a pilot's history, not just a single day's score
• Produces written, human-readable coaching notes and remediation suggestions — not just numbers
Page 8
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
• Runs only once there's enough history to say something meaningful
• Compute is switched on deliberately by the Training Director, as a cost-control measure
Page 9
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
6.5 Data Analysis — Micro, Macro & Trend Intelligence
This is the heart of what sets STRATOS apart from every alternative an airline might otherwise be using —
paper, Excel, or a generic ETR tool. All three of those can store a grade. None of them can turn that grade
into organizational intelligence the way STRATOS does, at three distinct levels of analysis:
Micro analysis — the single evaluation, examined closely
A category-by-category breakdown of one specific exam, automatically detecting whether that form uses
numeric or categorical scoring and presenting the result accordingly. This is the closest, most granular view
— exactly what happened in this one session, competency by competency.
Macro analysis — the cohort, compared side by side
A comparison across every pilot in a training group, class, rank, or aircraft type, using each pilot's latest
exam. Macro analysis is what instantly surfaces a shared weakness across a whole cohort — the difference
between “one pilot struggled” and “this entire class is weak on the same competency,” which points to a
training-program issue rather than an individual one.
• Template coverage view — which pilots have and haven't completed each training module, filterable
by rank
• A per-skill, per-attempt heatmap that automatically flags any skill with more than three borderline
results across a pilot's attempts
Trend analysis — the pilot, followed over time
A chronological view of a single pilot's full history on a given form, with per-skill and per-category pass
rates charted over time. This is what turns a series of disconnected evaluations into a visible trajectory —
improving, plateauing, or slipping — long before it would be obvious from looking at any single report.
• A dedicated Line Check (F-002) competency profile — methodology-level metrics computed across a
pilot's entire line-check history, not just their most recent result
Fleet-wide dashboards
Sitting above all three levels is a fleet-wide competency dashboard that bundles five analytical views into
one screen: key performance indicators, a pilot risk ranking, the competency distribution across the whole
fleet, a quarter-over-quarter trend, and examiner concordance — how consistently different examiners
grade against each other, so the Training Director can see if standards are being applied evenly across the
team.
Predictive risk flagging
Rather than making a Director scroll through every pilot's record to spot a problem, STRATOS
automatically surfaces only the pilots whose patterns suggest they need attention — turning analysis into a
short, actionable list instead of a wall of numbers.
Why this is the real differentiator
Grading and digital records are table stakes — any ETR tool or well-built spreadsheet can store a score.
Micro, macro, and trend analysis, examiner concordance, and predictive risk flagging are what turn
STRATOS from a records system into a genuine training-intelligence platform. This analytics layer is the
single biggest reason STRATOS replaces paper, Excel, and legacy ETR tools rather than just digitizing
Page 10
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
alongside them.
Page 11
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
6.6 Trainee Feedback Loop
After a training session, the Director can generate a short-lived QR code or link that the trainee scans — no
login required. The trainee rates their ground and simulator training experience and can leave free-text
comments, tied to the specific instructor and aircraft type. Directors see all this feedback rolled up in a
dedicated dashboard.
• No account or password needed for trainees to give feedback
• Links expire automatically for security (24 hours by default)
• Feedback closes the loop between how training is delivered and how it's graded
6.7 Notifications
A live notification system alerts relevant users — within their own department — when something needs
attention: a new evaluation has been processed, an AI coaching summary is ready, or a result needs follow-
up.
6.8 Administration & Security
• Create, activate, and remove Examiner and Director accounts, with a clear “pending” state for new
users awaiting department assignment
• Pilot data and cabin-crew data are kept structurally separate at the database level — not just hidden in
the interface — so a security review or an auditor gets a real, verifiable answer about data isolation
• Secure login is handled by a dedicated, managed authentication service rather than a custom-built login
system
• A Director-only switch controls whether the AI Assistant's compute is running, as a deliberate cost-
control measure

STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
7. What Makes This Different — Beyond Grading and Records
It's easy to describe STRATOS as “digital forms plus grading” and stop there — but that undersells what
actually separates it from paper, Excel, and legacy ETR tools:
• Built native to the methodology, not adapted to it: every screen, rule, and data field traces back to
the EBT/CBTA framework itself, rather than a generic system with competencies bolted on.
• Analysis at three altitudes: micro (single exam), macro (cohort), and trend (individual pilot over
time) — the depth of analysis no spreadsheet or paper file can offer (Section 6.5).
• From individual grade to organizational intelligence: a single evaluation becomes part of a fleet-
wide picture the moment it's submitted, instead of sitting in a folder or a spreadsheet tab.
• Built around the airline's own manual and forms: onboarding fits the platform to the airline's
existing standards, not the other way around (Section 5).
• Consistency: every grade is calculated the same way, every time, removing the person-to-person and
spreadsheet-formula variation common elsewhere.
• Speed: a polished report exists the instant a form is submitted — no manual write-up or re-typing.
• Foresight: predictive risk flagging and AI coaching summaries surface problems before they become
bigger issues, rather than waiting for someone to notice.
• Accountability: examiner-to-examiner grading consistency (concordance) is tracked, so standards can
be verified as being applied evenly.
• Already multi-line-of-business: pilot and cabin-crew evaluation run on the same platform today, with
real data separation between departments.
• Regulator-facing from day one: audit readiness isn't a feature bolted on before an inspection — it's a
byproduct of how every record is captured (Section 1.2).
• Built for the safety culture the methodology demands: EBT/CBTA exists to move training away
from punitive pass/fail checks; STRATOS is built to protect that intent in how results are surfaced and
used.

8. Current Status — Honest Picture
STRATOS is live and in daily production use, but it is not yet a fully complete EBT/CBTA system end-to-
end. This section is here so the handbook stays accurate rather than promotional. EBT/CBTA is a voluntary
upgrade path in Egypt today, not yet a regulatory mandate — so STRATOS is positioned commercially as
an operational improvement airlines can choose to adopt, not as a compliance requirement.

9. What's Coming Next
1. Full migration of F-003 onto the same nine-competency model already live on F-001 and F-002.
2. Digital signatures on all forms — a real captured-signature-and-lock step for TRE/TRI, trainee, and
inspector sign-off.
3. Automatic certification-expiry (“recurrency”) tracking, so a pilot's next required check is flagged
automatically instead of tracked manually.
Page 14
STRATOS EBT/CBTA Platform Handbook
4. Support for a second airline client, which requires separating data by airline (not just by department)
inside the system — the main technical step to onboarding beyond the first customer.
5. A bounded scheduling layer — assigning a pilot to a simulator slot, instructor, and date — without
turning STRATOS into a full resourcing/rostering product.
10. Glossary
• EBT: Evidence-Based Training — ICAO's competency-focused training and evaluation methodology.
• CBTA: Competency-Based Training and Assessment — IATA's parallel methodology.
• ETR: Electronic Training Records — the precise product category for STRATOS today.
• TEM: Threat & Error Management — tracking how crew identify and handle threats and errors during
a session.
• Just Culture: the non-punitive safety philosophy EBT/CBTA is built on — evaluation data is used to
identify training needs, not to assign blame.
• Concordance: how consistently different examiners grade the same competencies against each other
— the standardization signal a Training Director and a regulator both look for.
• IOSA / ECAA / GACA: IOSA is IATA's operational safety audit; ECAA and GACA are the Egyptian
and Saudi civil aviation regulators. All three are the kinds of audits STRATOS's records are built to
answer.
• TRE / TRI: Type Rating Examiner / Type Rating Instructor — qualified examiners who conduct and
sign off evaluations.
• S1–S5: The five-band grading scale STRATOS uses, from S1 (Unsatisfactory, below 70%) to S5
(Excellent, above 95%).
• Micro / Macro / Trend analysis: STRATOS's three analytical altitudes — a single exam, a cohort
comparison, and a pilot's history over time (Section 6.5).
• LMS: Learning Management System — delivers e-learning courses. STRATOS is not an LMS.
• TMS: Training Management System — handles scheduling and rostering. STRATOS is not yet a full
TMS.
